chapter: Harlem musicians and the road with Armstrong
title: Breakdowns, blowouts in Mississippi and missing a dance
summary: Bus blowouts on half-gravel roads led to hired cars, and Holmes's car went a hundred miles the wrong way and missed the dance.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: What about the breakdowns? The buses...?
Oh yeah, we had them, too.

Everything happened. Yes, we had it all happen. We was in Mississippi, and half the road was paved and the other half was gravel. And boy, we had more blowouts on that road. Oh, brother, did we have some blowouts.

So we got to one town, Monroe, I think it was...Monroe, Louisiana or somewhere down there. We had to hire some cars... We had to hire some cars to get where we were going, you know. So we get in the cars, and the cars got split up. So I don't know, maybe I'm ahead of my story. I know the car I was in went a hundred miles in the wrong direction And when we found out where we were at, went in the wrong direction... I think it was time for the dance to start then. Now, we're a hundred miles in the wrong direction from where we were at. Well, we never made that dance. I don't know how the people carried on. But there was about five or six of us in that car. We didn't make that dance. The rest of the band was there. I guess they did the best they could.
Yeah. Well, I mean, as long as he's there, that's all they need anyway. They were satisfied as long as he's there. But if he's not there, you'd better get out of town.
